prompt: Production sprite sheet for an atmospheric, slightly abandoned 2D pixel-art neighborhood RPG. Exactly FOUR separated architectural entrance sprites in a regular 2 by 2 grid, 384x384 per cell, total 768x768. Pure solid magenta background, no checkerboard, no captions, no letters, no humans, no furniture, no extra panels. Top-left: FRONT OPEN. Top-right: same FRONT CLOSED. Bottom-left: SIDE OPEN. Bottom-right: same SIDE CLOSED. Same dimensions for each open/closed pair. Restrained weathered olive, warm plaster, muted grey masonry, small tarnished brass accents. Hand-placed readable pixel clusters, granular worn surfaces, subtle old cracks and edge highlights, no painterly smooth gradients or heavy black cartoon outlines. In each cell keep at least 35px clear magenta margin. Camera is high orthographic RPG cutaway view, about 55 degrees down from horizontal, axes aligned to screen, no vanishing point and NO isometric diamond geometry. FRONT entrance belongs to a horizontal wall: broad top surfaces, compressed vertical facade, threshold along bottom. SIDE entrance belongs to a vertical wall on the LEFT of a street: travel is horizontal left-right. Show the wall cutaway/top surfaces of the north and south piers, deep horizontal threshold connecting to street on RIGHT, building interior on LEFT. It must visually belong IN THE WALL, not a freestanding portal, not a fence on paving. Do NOT turn the front facade 90 degrees. Side vertical facade is edge-on; never draw a frontal door panel facing the camera in the side entrance. Keep opening at the center of the wall segment. C: SMALL COVERED VESTIBULE. An inviting but abandoned little recessed entry, with short mossy stone steps flush to the sill (not a staircase), substantial chipped plaster/brick side cheeks, shallow wooden overhang with old zinc flashing. In OPEN state a modest door leaf has folded completely into the building and is largely invisible; darkness and threshold invite passage. CLOSED state same entrance with plain faded charcoal wooden door blocking it. Front view includes a broad visible top of modest overhang and wall returns. SIDE view must be mostly a little ROOF-NOTCH and HORIZONTAL SHADOWED PASSAGE tucked INTO the vertical building on LEFT; a small overhead zinc/wood lintel slab and plaster corners, paving extending to RIGHT. Wall-plane sides are north/south of opening. No freestanding pillars, no wooden railing, no long corridor, no huge ornate arch. CLOSED side uses narrow north-south dark wooden slab at the back of recess. Whole entrance should read as part of a building mass, softly shadowed and practical.
